sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].

FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an $8.3 billion impairment charge [F13][D97][X112], which the filings attribute to Shave Care goodwill and Gillette intangible write-downs after currency devaluations and slower grooming category growth [P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% to $15.7 billion, $8.3 billion of the increase being the base-period impairment charge [F14][D148][P71].
The recent pace is slower: revenue compounded at 2.0% over FY2023 to FY2026, with FY2025 up only 0.3% before a 3.3% rebound in FY2026 [D664][D406][D457].
In FY2026, Non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth and the US only 0.1pp, lifting Non-US back to 52.0% of revenue [D511][D457][D536][D509].
The filing attributes the 3% sales increase to favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
By segment, Fabric & Home Care added 0.8pp and Beauty 1.3pp in FY2026, while Baby, Feminine & Family Care added just 0.2pp [D543][D603][D564].
Operating income fell 3.4% in FY2026 against revenue growth of 3.3%, and operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue [D458][D457][D482].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% in FY2026 against net income growth of 0.5%, helped by a 1.3% reduction in the diluted share count [D461][D459][D476].
The FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high [F30][D648][D647].

The 1.6pp operating-margin decline came mostly from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp) [D470][D483][D485], which the filing attributes to lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [P25].
Gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix, partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings, while SG&A rose on marketing spending [P5].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, as other income of $1.1 billion and a 20.8% tax rate cushioned the gap [F50][F30][X108][D443].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, below the 1.02x free-cash-flow window median [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
The 9.8% operating-cash-flow increase came as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with inventory consuming $641 million and payables generating $919 million [D462][P3].
Free-cash-flow margin of 17.4% was above the 17.2% window median, with capex at 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A [D441][D654][D440][D446].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, and investing cash flow used $4.6 billion, primarily for capital expenditures and hedge settlements [D464][F90][F110][P2].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, net cash of -27.8% of revenue, against a -1.0% peer median and a 33rd percentile among six staples peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median and near the 0.63x low, with working capital of -$12.5 billion [F180][D663][D661][F170].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, down from 116.6% in FY2025 [X134][X144][D453][D402].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D468][F190][D476].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in FY2026 at 0.68x, the latest point in a window that never exceeded 0.88x [R1][F180][D662].
This reflects a negative working-capital model rather than distress, but it leaves little liquidity cushion if payables terms tighten [F170].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% [R2][D402][D453].
Payout now matches free cash flow almost exactly, so any further free-cash-flow dip would force the buyback to shrink or debt to rise [D453].
If the FY2027 operating margin falls below the 22.1% window median, the FY2026 margin erosion would be confirmed rather than reversed, in the FY2027 10-K [D648].
If free cash flow divided by net income falls below the 1.02x window median, cash conversion would be weakening, in the FY2027 10-K [D660].
If buybacks plus dividends rise back above the 116.6% of free cash flow seen in FY2025, the payout would again outrun cash generation, in the FY2027 10-K [D402].
